decision.reason: The unchanged realized-posture variable is incompatible with a pre-contact predictor on all 22 entries; no complete two-field row exists. This is a semantic/time-use finding, not evidence that prior intentions cannot be researched.
decision.next_design_requirement: A fortification-only profile would need to model source-reporting/missingness explicitly, define coextensive force/target rows, source/coding sensitivities and grouped evaluation before a separately authorized fit. A planned-posture variable would require a separate definition and evidence audit.
decision.stop: Stop this complete-group audit. No wider extraction, new sources, fit, feature release or final-set use follows.

observations.interpretation: Proposed-use findings only. All original supported claims remain descriptive evidence. No production admission validator or release is implemented.

inspection.image_limit: Only listed images were visually re-inspected in this audit. Other registered facsimiles remain byte-bound earlier records; inspection of their cited text is not a new image inspection.
inspection.independence_limit: Nine registered author/family groups across the whole campaign are not nine independent witnesses per entry. Original dependency notes remain in the frozen source snapshot; no votes or corroboration weights.
inspection.verification_limit: Exact text/metadata/raw bindings establish linkage, not historical truth. Reading is primary only, with no separate or independent review.

entries.anchor: Initial French attack on the outposts at Gottmannshofen, before the Zusam bridge/town and heights actions.
entries.area: Gottmannshofen–Wertingen–Roggden, with the initial outpost screen retained.
entries.fortification_note: The town gates, bridge, heights and woods occur at different stages. The passages do not describe both initial positions at the outpost contact; town gates alone do not establish defended walls.

entries.anchor: Firing at the Danube bridges before the French crossing and later bridgehead defence.
entries.area: Bridges/island at Günzburg and the later heights; Reisensburg proposals are separate.
entries.fortification_note: The descriptions mix bridge firing, island, crossing and later defensive heights. The order to make abatis/entrenchments at Reisensburg follows a crossing and does not establish executed opening works. The existing none_named cannot cover both opening positions.

entries.anchor: French arrival/encounter near Haslach; French and Krauss accounts differ on the subsequent attack roles.
entries.area: Haslach–Jungingen and the Austrian Böfingen/Örlingen/Spitzberg dispositions; no selected opening footprint.
entries.fortification_note: The French account names artillery in Spitzberg works and deployments from entrenchments; Krauss records Bianchi inspecting entrenchments in the morning but names no works fought from. This is not a clean physical-presence contradiction: use, place and the moving engagement force must be mapped before either existing code is applied at first contact. No vote selects an account.

entries.anchor: No securely established first hostile-contact anchor for the frozen Parsdorf entry.
entries.area: Pursuit toward Parsdorf and the distinct main army at Anzing.
entries.fortification_note: The battalion is reported to surrender without a blow while the charging cavalry is still at a distance. That charge/surrender is a possible no-shot hostile-contact anchor; the boundary does not require an exchange of fire. However, captures in the preceding rear-guard pursuit supply an earlier possible contact whose inclusion in the frozen action remains unresolved. The cited positions cannot cover both alternatives without choosing a new local-only scope. The journal section has no established document date; the following letter date is not borrowed.

entries.anchor: Bridge contact/cannonade precedes the crossing, village and abbey attacks.
entries.area: Danube bridge and upper Elchingen/abbey are distinct positions.
entries.fortification_note: The abbey enclosure and later defence are named; Krauss records its occupation in response to the approaching threat, but the cited ordering does not put that occupation securely before the initial bridge contact. Loison’s retranchés behind the first houses may mean cover rather than constructed works. The positive and none_named descriptions remain; the field is blocked for timing/scope, not a finding of physical absence.

entries.anchor: Investment on 13 October and artillery fire on 14 October precede capitulation; the frozen entry does not settle the hostile-contact start.
entries.area: Memmingen town/front/gates and investing forces.
entries.fortification_note: Spangen’s reported weak entrenchments and Soult’s order to continue Austrian works establish reported works, but not when construction/occupation began relative to the investment’s first contact. Soult’s half-fortified post also concerns its prospective use. Kein fester Platz does not mean no works. Retain the unknown opening mapping.

entries.anchor: Daytime pursuit/combat near Albeck and Eselsburg precedes a distinct night Herbrechtingen position.
entries.area: Day movement and the later crenellated town wall at Herbrechtingen.
entries.fortification_note: The French account places defenders at the crenellated wall in the night action; the other account describes day positions without works. The frozen engagement does not resolve a day-only/night-only footprint. Selecting the later wall as the opening would silently choose a new boundary.

entries.anchor: The 17 October capitulation label is distinct from the 15 October assaults and later town enclosure.
entries.area: Michelsberg/Geisberg advanced works and Ulm town are successive positions.
entries.fortification_note: Occupied advanced redoubts before the 15 October assault and surviving town walls are reported. That does not define the first hostile contact belonging to the frozen capitulation entry. The audit does not substitute the 15 October assault or assume that every earlier operation belongs to this row; its boundary/area remains blocked.

entries.anchor: Klein’s column is explicitly said to meet the enemy first at Neresheim, after its morning departure.
entries.area: French approaching column and Austrian initial heights north of the Egau by the wood/church and ditch/road bridge.
entries.fortification_note: The approach and both initial dispositions are described before the reported attack. No works are named in those descriptions. The church and ditch are not thereby defensive works; later Ohmenheim woods and squares are not used to infer an opening absence. Eligible only as a source-reporting category.

entries.anchor: Bridge attack/petard is the reported opening; Koch’s night of 17 October and the 18 October dating remain alternatives.
entries.area: Castel Vecchio/bridge and occupied Campagnola works on the opposing bank.
entries.fortification_note: Koch describes recently prepared Castel Vecchio, guns/bastion and barricaded bridge, and the Archduke’s prebuilt works occupied by Auffenberg companies before the attack narrative. Both named-positive sides survive either relative date ordering. Disobeyed/non-occupation instructions do not erase the account of actual occupation. This does not measure the proportion of either force protected.

entries.anchor: Pursuit/convoy contacts, a night encounter, the plateau stand and parley are alternative parts of the local sequence.
entries.area: Route from Neresheim/Ohmenheim to the Trochtelfingen plateau; no newly selected local boundary.
entries.fortification_note: The plateau position is a later stand and the pursuit is already in progress. The existing descriptions do not give both positions at an agreed first contact belonging to this capitulation entry. None_named remains a later description, not opening zeros.

entries.anchor: Initial rearguard contact beyond Nuremberg precedes Heroldsberg/Geschaid/Eschenau/Forth.
entries.area: A moving pursuit across several localities, rather than only the last position.
entries.fortification_note: The existing code summarizes successive town, defile, height and wood positions. Both initial rearguard and approaching positions are not described at one mapped contact. Later descriptions with no works named do not fill that gap.

entries.anchor: Opening 29 October actions near Verona/San Michele precede the main attacks on the Caldiero line.
entries.area: The whole frozen 29–31 October engagement, including the already-held Caldiero line beyond the forward posts.
entries.fortification_note: Angeli’s prelude places the army waiting in its positions by 23 October, describes earlier entrenchment construction and the standing occupation of Caldiero. The named works need not be at the first outpost hit: they belong to a reported held position within the engagement before that contact. Later redoubt assaults support realized use but are not the temporal basis. Eligible B named-positive category; the other side’s physical absence is unknown. This basis includes OCR-only passages.

entries.anchor: Initial fight of Hillinger’s force, followed by a French retreat and later renewed action.
entries.area: Pojano positions and the later rally at the breached château of San Felice.
entries.fortification_note: The none_named claim concerns positions fought from, while a breached castle appears as a later rally point. It is not established whether those works were held in the relevant opening dispositions. No opening no-works category or physical absence can be inferred from the later non-use description.

entries.anchor: Assaults at the Tyrolean barriers: Moriggl’s 4 November and Victoires’ 5 November accounts are retained.
entries.area: Scharnitz/Leutasch barriers; later Seefeld captures are a different phase.
entries.fortification_note: The passages describe held fortifications and wall positions before the assaults. The named-positive B category is invariant to the retained 4/5 November alternatives. The Alpl redoubt/abatis suggestion is counterfactual, not an executed work, and natural rocky batteries are not constructed fortifications. No claim covers the whole army behind works.

entries.anchor: Neuhaus/Gaming clashes precede the retreat to Mariazell and the later castle occupation.
entries.area: Initial approach/retreat and Mariazell–St Sigmund positions, kept distinct.
entries.fortification_note: Schönhals explicitly places the occupation of Schloss St Sigmund to secure a retreat after fighting has begun; that positive claim is excluded for this boundary. The Alombert/Colin none_named account does not map both initial positions and differs in place/function detail. One excluded later state does not convert the remaining unknown into an opening absence.

entries.anchor: Russian attack on French outposts in the morning precedes daytime and evening encirclement actions.
entries.area: Dürnstein–Loiben, initial pickets/bivouacs and the later walled roads/ruins.
entries.fortification_note: Castle-ruin pickets at the beginning and walls/ruins in the evening have different functions and times. The claim that no works were fought from does not classify the opening named-works positions without resolving those functions. The posture alternatives remain source dependent, including Kotzebue/relation ancestry; they are not extra witnesses or extra rows.

entries.anchor: Bregenz outpost fighting on 13 November and Dornbirn contact on 14 November precede the capitulation.
entries.area: Outposts at Bregenz/Dornbirn, Moriggl’s main position at Hohenems and Victoires’ main body at Feldkirch.
entries.fortification_note: Moriggl’s construction of Hohenems entrenchments on 5 November is pre-contact, not an automatically late state. However, the two accounts locate the main body differently and the frozen capitulation row lacks a settled operational area/starting contact. The applicability of those works to this row is unresolved; none_named in the other account is not evidence against their physical existence. Both candidates remain blocked, rather than selecting the last outpost or taking a source vote.

entries.anchor: Cavalry skirmishing precedes the grenadier/Legrand attacks on the main position.
entries.area: Initial cavalry contacts and the later defended position beyond the defile.
entries.fortification_note: The existing none_named describes the main defended position and later attacks, without both initial cavalry positions. It cannot stand for a source-qualified two-side opening description; no physical absence is coded.

entries.anchor: Angeli’s 24 November encounter after the march toward Noale; Koch’s 4 December dawn orders remain a materially different calendar/scope.
entries.area: Castelfranco, Noale road and Campo San Pietro accounts are not silently merged.
entries.fortification_note: The accounts differ in date, column routes and phase. Town entry follows a rout and does not establish defended town works at the opening. The none_named descriptions cannot be mapped to one common pre-contact footprint; no date correction or majority vote is made.

entries.anchor: Opening outpost/battle contacts on 2 December, with the reported French dispositions and Santon preparation already in place.
entries.area: Whole reported Austerlitz position, including Santon beyond the initial right-flank contact.
entries.fortification_note: Victoires places the fortified and occupied Santon in the pre-battle deployment; it is an A named-positive condition before contact even though the first action is elsewhere. Abandoned show retrenchments and the natural ditch at Telnitz do not supply this code. Earlier preparation may be a commander-created mediator: eligibility for a descriptive prediction design supplies no causal credit.

entries.anchor: The 5 December general attack after Lindenau’s quiet outpost inspection; the 1–4 December skirmishes are retained as earlier events.
entries.area: Initial Steken market/heights/outpost line and assembling Austrian columns toward Wonau.
entries.fortification_note: Völderndorff gives the defended positions and immediately prior outpost inspection; Schönhals gives the assembled attacking columns before the 5 December attack. Neither initial position description names works. The earlier 3 December action is not selected as this entry’s start. Eligible as none_named reporting only, with actual absence and protection unknown.
